sets.relationshipLabel: a creature and the thing that belongs to it
sets.explanation: Each creature is defined by the thing it guards or lives in — a dragon's hoard, a fox's den.

sets.relationshipLabel: a humble or cursed origin transformed by magic into its result
sets.explanation: Magic turns a lowly origin into its grander result — pumpkin becomes carriage, frog becomes prince.

sets.relationshipLabel: a kind of figure and one of them by name
sets.explanation: Each named figure is simply a specific instance of the broader fairy-tale role above it.

sets.relationshipLabel: the one property or utterance a magical thing can never have
sets.explanation: Each object's magic is defined by the very thing it categorically lacks — dust with no weight, a mirror that cannot lie.

glossary.definition: A wild-haired old woman from Slavic folktales who lives deep in the forest in a hut that stands on chicken legs.

definitions.definition: A huge fire-breathing beast with scales and wings, often found sleeping on piles of treasure.
A big secret stash of treasure someone's been collecting and guarding for ages.
A clever, quick little forest animal with a bushy tail, known for sneaking around at night.
A cozy hidden burrow or hideout where a wild animal sleeps and shelters.
A big round orange vegetable that grows on a vine, often carved or used in autumn cooking.
An elegant horse-drawn vehicle used for fancy travel, especially to balls and palaces.
A small green hopping creature that lives near water and croaks at night.
A young royal man, next in line to a throne, often the hero in old stories.
A young royal woman, daughter or wife of royalty, often the star of fairy tales.
A kind girl forced into servitude by her stepfamily who gets a magical night out at the ball.
A woman with magical powers, sometimes helpful, sometimes wicked, who casts spells.
A wild-haired old woman from Slavic folktales who lives deep in the forest in a hut that stands on chicken legs.
A shimmering magical powder that lets things (or people) fly when sprinkled on them.
How heavy something is — the pull gravity has on it.
An enchanted looking-glass that can speak and answer questions truthfully.
A statement that isn't true — a lie or something made up to deceive.
